pieces.title: The pieces
pieces.desc: Meet the board and learn how every piece moves.

rules.title: The rules
rules.desc: Capturing, check, checkmate, castling and the other special rules.

board.title: The chessboard
board.intro: The chessboard has **64 squares**, light and dark in turn. It always lies so that the square in the **bottom right corner is light** – it's marked here.
board.intro_kid: This is a chessboard! It has 64 squares – light ones and dark ones, always taking turns. Look at the corner at the bottom right: it's light. That's how the board always lies.
board.names: The columns are called **files**, from **a** to **h**. The rows are called **ranks**, from **1** to **8**. Every square is named by its file and rank: the marked square is **e4** – file e, rank 4. The letters and numbers are printed along the edge of the board.
board.names_kid: Every square has a name, like a seat in the cinema! The letter (a to h) tells you the column, the number (1 to 8) the row. The marked square is called e4. Look at the letters and numbers at the edge of the board.
board.setup: This is how a game starts. White is at the bottom and always makes the **first move**. The pawns stand in front; behind them, from left to right: rook, knight, bishop, queen, king, bishop, knight, rook.
board.setup_kid: Here's how all the pieces stand at the start. White is at the bottom and always goes first. The little pawns stand in the front row, the big pieces behind them.
board.queen: A handy rule: the queen starts on **her own colour** – the white queen on a light square, the black queen on a dark one. Tap the white queen.
board.queen_kid: The queen likes her own colour: the white queen stands on a light square. Can you find her? Tap her!
board.king: The two kings face each other on the same file. Tap the **black king**.

rook.title: The rook
rook.desc: Straight lines, as far as it likes.
rook.intro: The **rook** moves in straight lines: forwards, backwards, left or right – as many squares as it likes. It cannot jump over other pieces.
rook.intro_kid: The rook is like a racing car on straight roads: forwards, backwards, left, right – as far as it wants! But it can't jump over other pieces.
rook.s1: Move the rook to the star to collect it.
rook.s1_kid: Drive the rook to the star!
rook.s2: Collect both stars. How few moves do you need?
rook.s3: Your own pawns are in the way, and the rook can't jump over them. Collect both stars.
rook.s3_kid: The pawns are walls – the rook has to drive around them. Get both stars!

bishop.title: The bishop
bishop.desc: Diagonal lines – and always the same colour.
bishop.intro: The **bishop** moves diagonally, as far as it likes. That's why it always stays on squares of **one colour**: this bishop stands on a dark square and will never reach a light one.
bishop.intro_kid: The bishop only walks diagonally, like down a slide. That's why it always stays on its own colour: this one lives on the dark squares.
bishop.s1: Collect the star with the bishop.
bishop.s3: This bishop lives on the light squares. Collect all three stars.
bishop.color: Can this bishop ever reach the marked square **d4**?
bishop.color_done: Right! This bishop stands on a light square and always stays on light squares – d4 is dark.

queen.title: The queen
queen.desc: The strongest piece: rook and bishop in one.
queen.intro: The **queen** is the strongest piece. She moves like a rook and a bishop together: straight **and** diagonally, as far as she likes.
queen.intro_kid: The queen is the superhero of chess! She can go straight like the rook and diagonally like the bishop – in every direction, as far as she wants.
queen.s1: Collect both stars with the queen.
queen.s2: Four stars – find the shortest way!
queen.s3: Mind your own pawns. Collect all three stars.

king.title: The king
king.desc: The most important piece – one step at a time.
king.intro: The **king** is the most important piece: if he is trapped, the game is lost. He moves just **one square**, in any direction.
king.intro_kid: The king is the most important piece – you have to protect him! He's a bit slow: he walks only one step at a time, but in any direction.
king.s1: Walk the king to both stars.
king.danger: The king may **never** move to a square that an enemy piece attacks – he would be captured there. The black rook attacks the whole 5th rank.
king.danger_kid: Careful! The king must never step onto a square an enemy piece is aiming at. The black rook guards the whole red line.
king.where: Tap every square the white king **can** move to.
king.s2: The black knight guards some squares, so the king can't step on them. Collect both stars anyway.

knight.title: The knight
knight.desc: The jumper: an L-shape over everything.
knight.intro: The **knight** moves in an **L-shape**: two squares straight, then one to the side. It is the only piece that may **jump** over other pieces.
knight.intro_kid: The knight jumps like a horse, in an L: two steps straight, one step to the side – hop! It's the only piece that can jump over others.
knight.where: The knight is surrounded, but it simply jumps over. Tap every square it can land on.
knight.s2: The knight jumps right over the pawns. Collect all three stars.
knight.s3: Sometimes the knight needs a detour. Get it to the star as quickly as you can!
knight.s3_kid: The star is right next door, but the knight has to hop around. Can you find the way?

pawn.title: The pawn
pawn.intro: The **pawn** moves forwards only, one square at a time. From its starting square it may also move **two squares** at once. It can never move backwards.
pawn.intro_kid: The pawn is small but brave: it only walks forwards, one step at a time. On its very first move it may take a big two-step jump.
pawn.s1: Collect both stars with the pawn.
pawn.capture: Pawns capture differently from how they move: **one square diagonally forwards**. A piece directly in front blocks the pawn – it can't capture straight ahead.
pawn.capture_kid: Pawns walk straight but capture diagonally! And if something stands right in front of a pawn, it's stuck.
pawn.s2: The way ahead is blocked. Capture your way to both stars!
pawn.where: Where can this pawn go? Tap every square it can move to or capture on.

capture.title: Capturing
capture.desc: Take enemy pieces off the board.
capture.intro: Every piece **except the pawn** captures the way it moves: it moves onto the square of an enemy piece and takes it off the board. (The pawn captures diagonally, as you saw.) You can never capture your own pieces.
capture.intro_kid: Capturing means your piece moves onto the square of an enemy piece and knocks it off the board!
capture.s1: Capture all the black pieces with the rook.
capture.s2: Now with the knight: capture all three pawns.
capture.safe: You can take the bishop or the knight. One of them is **protected**: another black piece could take back if you capture it. Capture the **unprotected** one!
capture.safe_kid: You can take the bishop or the knight. But one of them has a bodyguard! Take the one that's all alone.
capture.safe_done: Right! Nothing guarded the knight. Had you taken the bishop, the pawn on e6 would have captured your queen.

check.title: Check
check.intro: When a piece attacks the king, the king is in **check**. The player in check must end it immediately – no other move is allowed. Here the white rook gives check along the e-file.
check.intro_kid: When a piece aims at the king, that's called check! The king must get out of danger right away.
check.give3: Even a pawn can give check. Try it!

escape.title: Getting out of check
escape.desc: Three ways out: move, block, capture.
escape.intro:
There are three ways out of check:
1. **Move** the king to a safe square.
2. **Block**: put a piece in between.
3. **Capture** the attacking piece.
Which one works depends on the position.
escape.intro_kid: Your king is in check – what now? Three ideas: run away, put a piece in the way, or capture the attacker!
escape.run: Your king is in check and has no helpers. Move him to a safe square.
escape.block: The king can't step away – but you can put a piece in between.
escape.take: A knight gives check. A knight's check can't be blocked – capture it!

checkmate.title: Checkmate
checkmate.desc: Check with no way out wins the game.
checkmate.intro: If the king is in check and there is **no way out** – no free square, nothing to put in between, nothing to capture – it is **checkmate**. The game is over, and whoever gives checkmate wins. Here Black is checkmated: Black's own pawns block the king's escape.
checkmate.intro_kid: Checkmate is the goal of the game! The king is in check and can't escape anywhere. Then the game is over – and whoever gives checkmate wins!
checkmate.q1_done: Right – no mate. The king can escape to h7.
checkmate.q2: And this one – is Black checkmated?
checkmate.q2_done: Right! The queen gives check, the white king protects her, and every square around the black king is covered.
checkmate.m1: Checkmate the black king in one move!
checkmate.m2: Checkmate in one move with the queen.
checkmate.m3: One more: checkmate in one move.

castling.title: Castling
castling.desc: King to safety, rook into play – in one move.
castling.intro: Once per game you may **castle**: the king moves **two squares** towards a rook, and the rook moves to the king's other side, right next to him. That tucks your king away safely and brings a rook into the game. This is **short castling**, towards the **kingside** – the side where the king starts.
castling.intro_kid: Castling is a special move: the king takes two steps sideways, and the rook walks around him to his other side. Now the king sits safely in his castle!
castling.short: Castle short! Move the king two squares to the right (or drop him on the rook) – the rook comes along by itself.
castling.long: Now castle **long**, towards the **queenside** – the side where the queen starts: the king moves two squares to the left.
castling.rules:
This is **long** castling. You may only castle if:
• the king and that rook have **not moved** yet,
• there is **nothing** between them,
• the king is **not in check**, and doesn't pass over or land on an **attacked square**.
castling.why: Why is White **not** allowed to castle short here?
castling.why_through: The king would pass over an attacked square
castling.why_blocked: A piece is in the way
castling.why_done: Right! The black bishop attacks f1 – the square the king has to pass over. So short castling isn't allowed.

en-passant.title: En passant
en-passant.intro: A special rule: if an enemy pawn moves **two squares** and lands **right next to** your pawn, you may capture it as if it had moved only one square. This is called **en passant** (French for “in passing”). Watch: Black plays d7–d5, and White captures on d6.
en-passant.intro_kid: A secret pawn trick! If an enemy pawn jumps two squares and lands right next to your pawn, your pawn may still capture it – as if it had taken only one step.
en-passant.ep1: Black has just played d7–d5. Capture en passant!
en-passant.ep2: Now you're Black. White has just played c2–c4 – capture en passant!
en-passant.when: Say you missed the moment and played a different move first. May you still capture en passant afterwards?
en-passant.when_done: Right! En passant is only allowed on the very next move – after that the chance is gone.

promotion.title: Promotion
promotion.desc: A pawn on the last rank becomes a new piece.
promotion.intro: When a pawn reaches the **last rank**, it is promoted at once: it becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight – you choose. Almost always you take a **queen**.
promotion.intro_kid: When a pawn walks all the way to the other side, it transforms – into a queen, for example! A little pawn becomes the strongest piece.
promotion.queen: Push the pawn forward and make it a queen!
promotion.mate: Promote – and give checkmate at the same time!

draw.title: Draws and stalemate
draw.stalemate: If the player to move has **no legal move** but is **not in check**, it's **stalemate** – a **draw**, even though one side has far more material! Here Black is to move: the king isn't attacked, but every square next to it is.
draw.stalemate_kid: Stalemate is a trap for the winner! The king isn't in check, but it can't move anywhere – then the game is a draw, and nobody wins.
draw.q1: Black to move. Checkmate, stalemate, or neither?
draw.q1_done: Right – stalemate. The black king isn't in check, but all its squares are covered.
draw.q2_done: Right – checkmate! The king is in check, and the white king protects the queen.
draw.avoid: Checkmate in one move – but careful: lots of moves here would be stalemate!
draw.avoid_done: Checkmate! Moving the queen to c7 instead would have been stalemate – always check that the enemy king still has a move.
draw.other:
A game is also drawn when:
• the **same position** occurs **three times**,
• **50 moves** pass without a pawn move or a capture,
• neither side has enough material left to give checkmate – like here, king and bishop against king,
• or both players **agree** to a draw.

values.title: What are the pieces worth?
values.desc: What your pieces are worth – your material.
values.intro:
All your pieces together are your **material**. To judge a trade, players count them in points:
• pawn **1**
• knight **3**
• bishop **3**
• rook **5**
• queen **9**
The king has no price – losing him means losing the game.
values.intro_kid: Pieces are like coins with different values: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. The king is priceless!
values.q1_done: Right: a rook is worth 5, a bishop 3.
values.q2: You can trade your knight for the black rook. Is that a good deal?
values.q2_done: Yes! You give 3 points and get 5.
values.q3: Two bishops against a queen – who has more material?
values.q3_done: Right: the queen is worth 9, the two bishops together 6.
values.take: Your knight can capture a pawn or a rook. Take the more valuable piece!
values.take_done: Right – a rook is worth 5 points, a pawn only 1.

notation.title: Reading moves
notation.desc: How chess moves are written down.
notation.intro: Chess players write every move down. A move is the **piece letter** plus the **square** it goes to: **K** king, **Q** queen, **R** rook, **B** bishop, **N** knight. Pawns get no letter. Watch: **e4** (pawn to e4), **e5**, **Nf3** (knight to f3).
notation.intro_kid: Every chess move has a short name, like a secret code! A big letter says which piece moves (N for knight, B for bishop, R for rook, Q for queen, K for king), then comes the square. Pawns get no letter: e4 just means a pawn goes to e4.
notation.target: In the move **Nc3**, a knight goes to a square. Tap that square.
notation.target_kid: Nc3: the knight jumps to … which square? Tap it!
notation.symbols:
A few extra signs:
• **x** = captures: **Nxe5** – the knight captures on e5
• **+** = check, **#** = checkmate
• **O-O** = short castling, **O-O-O** = long castling
• **e8=Q** = the pawn promotes to a queen
• **1.** counts the moves; **…** before a move means Black played it (**1…e5**).
notation.q1: White plays **Nxe5**. What does that mean?
notation.q1_takes: The knight captures the piece on e5
notation.q1_moves: The knight moves to e5 without capturing
notation.q1_check: The knight gives check on e5
notation.q2: The last move was **Qxf7#**. What happened?
notation.q2_check: The queen captured on f7 – check, but the king can escape
notation.q2_mate: The queen captured on f7 – checkmate
notation.q2_moves: The queen moved to f7 without capturing
notation.q2_done: Right – **#** means checkmate. The king can't escape: the bishop on c4 protects the queen.
notation.play_done: That's Nf3 – you can read chess moves now.
